title: THE LAST CARTOGRAPHER
author: Annwesa Abhipsa Pani
text:
I trace the edges of their shadows
against walls that tremble with tomorrow,
mapping spaces I cannot reach,
the gaps where absence might arrive.
Death hums on a quiet train,
its ticket folded in another`s hand.
It stops too close,
stealing a voice, a gesture,
leaving only the hollow hum behind.
Every laugh is a grain of sand
slipping through a clock I cannot turn back.
Every glance a fragile coin
tossed into a well
that may swallow it silently,
leaving echoes to tremble in the dark.
I fear the silence
that would hollow my rooms,
the slow erasure of those I love,
the way a single absence
can bend the shape of all days.
I trace their lives
like maps drawn on fragile paper,
paths winding through streets and seasons,
paths that may vanish
in the blink of a night.
I want to memorize each line,
each laugh, each sigh,
before the ink fades into shadows.
Mortality is a hall of doors
I cannot open all at once.
I linger at the threshold,
clinging to the warmth of their presence,
writing maps of them
on walls that will outlast me,
for every page I may never turn.
And when the train comes,
quiet as a closing eyelid,
I hope the maps I made
are enough to carry them
through the spaces I cannot follow,
and that memory
becomes a room
where absence is only a shape
I have learned to honor.
